label: GO after an unrewarded rare transition, committing strongly to a1 (stay)
explanation: Fires almost only at GO (99% of mass; never at D2, a little at D1). Its core trigger is that the previous trial was a1 -> S2 (rare) and went unrewarded, so the model-based response is to stay with a1. The policy logit is strongly toward a1 (93% of mass has choice > 8). The feature essentially never fires after a2 or after a reward input. The narrow predicate GO & prev_action==1 & prev_common==0 & prev_reward==0 gets dev F1 0.76 and mass recall 0.80. Most of the missed mass is at the window first trial (rel -3), where the previous trial is outside the window (prev_common = -1). That is why the recorded predicate uses prev_common != 1 and requires a strong a1 policy (choice > 5): dev P 0.75, R 0.90, F1 0.82, mass recall 0.98. All variables are observed or are the agent own policy, so it uses no future variables. Magnitude is lower in the weakest quartile, which is partly common-unrewarded or late-context cases that the predicate covers less well (52% coverage of the bottom quartile versus 82% of the top). Residual false positives are rare-unrewarded a1 GO steps where the feature stays silent, mostly when the context had several recent rewards.

issues: Factual claims check out on dev. GO holds 99.1% of the activation mass, D1 0.9% (2086 steps) and D2 has 0 activations. prev_reward==1 has only 140 active steps (about 0% of mass). prev_action==2 holds 1.0% of mass. Choice >= 8.07 holds 93.1% of mass. The trigger is specific to a1 -> S2: GO & prev_reward==0 & prev_action==2 & prev_common==0 has 0 activations, and GO & prev_reward==0 & prev_action==1 & prev_common==1 & choice>5 has 0 of 9161 steps active.
Recorded predicate reproduces: dev P 0.751 / R 0.898 / F1 0.818 / mass recall 0.980; test P 0.739 / R 0.897 / F1 0.81 / mass recall 0.976.
The magnitude claim mixes up two predicates. '52% of the weakest quartile versus 82% of the top' is the narrow predicate. The recorded predicate covers [0.64, 0.96, 1.00, 1.00] by quartile.

choice>5 is effectively a proxy for the unknown previous trial at rel -3 (prev_common == -1), not a real condition. Within the a1-rare-unrewarded group it removes only 617 steps (precision 0.05 there). It matters only where the window hides the previous trial: GO & prev_reward==0 & prev_common==-1 has P 0.21 without it and P 0.60 with it. The rel -3 GO firing rate (0.064) matches the other positions, so the feature most likely fires on the same condition at rel -3 and the predicate simply cannot check it.

The leftover false positives lean in one direction. Among a1 -> S2 rare-unrewarded GO steps, the feature is silent more often when the two earlier trials were rewarded (precision 0.67, and almost none of the top-quartile mass) than when the trial two back was also unrewarded (precision 0.91, 37% of top-quartile coverage). So activation is modulated by a run of recent omitted rewards. This refines the label rather than refuting it: the feature still fires on most such steps.
Small scattered misses: weak activations (about 0.1-0.2 of max) at GO after a2 -> S2 common unrewarded, when the agent switches to a1. Their mass is negligible.
